content_groups.group_title: ACUTE EXACERBATION OF CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (AECOPD)

blocks.text: An acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) is an acute worsening of respiratory symptoms in a patient with COPD, beyond normal day-to-day variation, requiring a change in treatment.

items.text: Change in sputum colour or purulence.

blocks.text: AECOPD is commonly triggered by respiratory infections, air pollution and other environmental exposures.
The underlying mechanisms include increased airway inflammation, bronchoconstriction, mucus hypersecretion, airway oedema and worsening ventilation-perfusion mismatch.
Severe exacerbations may cause acute-on-chronic respiratory failure, hypercapnia, respiratory acidosis and cardiovascular complications.

blocks.text: **D. High-yield clinical pearls and examination points**
1. Diagnostic spirometry criterion
Post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC below 0.70.
2. Three cardinal symptoms
Increased dyspnoea, sputum volume and sputum purulence.
3. First-line bronchodilator
Salbutamol, with or without ipratropium.
4. Recommended corticosteroid regimen
Prednisolone 40 mg orally daily for 5 days.
5. Oxygen saturation target
88–92% in patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure.
6. Important ABG finding
Low pH with raised PaCO₂ indicates acute hypercapnic respiratory acidosis.
7. Indication for NIV
Persistent acute hypercapnic respiratory acidosis despite optimal medical therapy.
8. Antibiotic indication
Purulent sputum with other cardinal symptoms, or requirement for mechanical ventilation, among other relevant indications.
9. Important alternative diagnosis
Pulmonary embolism.
10. Aminophylline
Not routinely recommended because of its adverse-effect profile.
11. Important ventilation complication
Dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP.
12. Maintenance treatment
Long-acting bronchodilators, usually LABA/LAMA, with ICS added in selected patients according to exacerbation history, eosinophils and other indications.

2. NICE NG114: Antibiotic prescribing for acute COPD exacerbations, including antibiotic selection, doses, duration and IV-to-oral switching.
3. NICE NG115: Diagnosis and management of COPD in adults, including exacerbation prevention and long-term treatment.

Important 2026 update: GOLD continues to recommend short-acting bronchodilators as initial treatment, systemic corticosteroids for moderate/severe exacerbations for up to 5 days, and antibiotics selectively, generally for 5 days. NIV remains a key treatment for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure.
